title: Evaluation of nocturnal digital cough monitoring in people with chronic lung disease
summary:
In chronic lung diseases, cough is associated with the severity of the disease and is considered a sign of inadequate disease control and an early symptom of lung deterioration. The total cough frequency in 24 hours can be estimated very well from the nocturnal cough frequency.
The nocturnal cough frequency can be determined with modern cough monitor systems and provides much more accurate information than a patient interview. In this study, we use a cough monitor app that can record the nocturnal cough frequency in real time. So far, however, there is little data on continuous nocturnal measurement of cough frequency in patients with chronic lung diseases such as cystic fibrosis. 
This study will provide information on the daily variation of cough as an important symptom of chronic lung disease, which could help to better define what constitutes an exacerbation of lung disease (acute or chronic).
By establishing individual baseline values (cough frequency within normal variability) and threshold values for an increase in cough frequency, the basis for the use of continuous objective nocturnal cough monitoring in the care of patients with chronic lung disease is created.
The aim is to detect an incipient deterioration in lung function at an early stage so that therapy can be adjusted and possibly prevent hospitalization and prolonged deterioration in lung health. Cough monitoring could also help patients to adhere to treatment and self-manage their condition. Adoption into routine care is theoretically possible immediately after evaluation of the study data.

interventions.name: Patients with cystic fibrosis and healthy participants receive digital nocturnal cough monitoring using a smartphone app. This will be used to investigate the natural course of cough under standard therapy, evaluate possible influencing factors and evaluate its use as a warning system for pulmonary

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of Cystic Fibrosis
Availability of a smartphone
Exclusion criteria:
Comorbid condition likely to affect the patients cough frequency (e.g. post lung transplantation) or ability to adhere to monitoring.
The regular presence of a person of the same sex during nocturnal cough monitoring is also an exclusion criterion, as this may influence cough monitoring.
